messages:
ellie_support: Heads-up — SearchCorp opened a high-priority ticket: embeddings responses sometimes come back with dimension=1024 when their client expects 768, plus intermittent 3–12s latency spikes. They say the request endpoint was eu-west-1. Request IDs: r-az1:abc123, r-az1:def456. Happening since ~08:10 UTC. Any routing/capacity ideas? :warning:

alex_m: assigning. Can you paste the raw request/response for one of the failing IDs (headers + model name)? Also, did they recently change the model family in their config?

ellie_support: pasted snippets from customer — they call /v1/embeddings with model: "text-embed-001-v2" header "X-Region: eu-west-1". Response body for r-az1:abc123: `{"model":"text-embed-001-v1","embedding": [..1024 floats..], "dimension":1024}` — so model in response differs. Latency log: `2026-03-14T08:10:12Z r-az1:abc123 routed->us-east-1 coldstart=true queue_ms=4200 exec_ms=5200`.

nishant: grabbing infra logs now. I see routing decision recorded at router: `policy=region-preference, wanted=eu-west-1, chosen=us-east-1, reason=capacity-constraint, fallback_variant=embed-v1-1024`. Looks like when eu cluster is saturated we fallback to a compatible variant that has a different embedding dim (v1 = 1024). That explains dim mismatch.

infra-bot: [ALERT] embeddings-eu cluster (eu-west-1) CPU/GPU pending queue > 75% for 12m — autoscale attempts: 2, fallback routing active.

tim_engineering: confirmed — runtime currently treats v1/v2 as compatible fallback; but we shouldn't silently return a different embedding size. That's a bug. Two things: 1) for compatibility we must enforce model-variant compatibility map and reject with 409 when dims differ OR 2) perform transform/compat shim (not trivial). Immediate fix: stop routing to v1 for any request specifying model v2 with dimension expectation. I'll push a guard.

maria_net: on the networking side I see increased cross-region traffic from eu->us starting at 08:08 UTC, likely due to customer traffic spikes. BGP is fine; this is internal routing fallback.

alex_m: action items: (A) Support: ask SearchCorp to pin model version for now or set `prefer_region=true` header? (B) Infra: temporarily raise eu embed capacity (burst) and disable fallback to v1 variants for v2 requests. (C) Eng: patch runtime to return a clear error when fallback would change embedding dim.

sara_ops: customer is seeing billing surge because requests are routed to us-east high-cost nodes — they're asking for credit. I've put them on priority SLA. Repro steps requested by billing: curl sample + request_id.

ellie_support: repro steps I gave them: 1) Use this curl (they've already done it):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-001-v2","input":["test doc"]}'
```
Response we saw (trimmed):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"model":"text-embed-001-v1","embedding":[...],"dimension":1024}
```

nishant: repro locally by forcing eu cluster load: run the stress script on staging: `scripts/stress_embeddings --region eu-west-1 --qps 300 --model v2`. I reproduced fallback after ~2m and saw requests queued 3–6s. Batch size at the time was 64 which ballooned queueing. Lower batch_size helps latency but increases cost.

tim_engineering: quick mitigation deployed: disable cross-region fallback for embeddings when request specifies model family v2 (rollback if it causes errors). deploy-bot: rollback?

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-14T08:34:21Z — routing-guard v1.2 applied to staging then canary -> prod.

alex_m: infra, can you spin up 4x burst nodes in eu embed pool for next 2 hours and set autoscale aggressive? Also add short-term route override that pins SearchCorp's keys to eu nodes.

maria_net: done — bumped pool by 4 GPU nodes, route override in place for api-key: sk-prod-searchcorp (effective now). Monitoring latency and cross-region egress.

ellie_support: customer confirmed a drop in cross-region traffic after pinning, and embedding dims now consistently 768 for a few minutes. They still want root cause and preventive fix.

tim_engineering: next steps: (1) enforce model-variant compatibility in routing decision (error out instead of fallback), (2) add prefix/KV caching checks so hot models in a region don't coldstart on fallback, (3) add an explict header `X-Expected-Embedding-Dim` that the server validates and returns 409 on mismatch. I'll open PR and tag @nishant for infra tests.

nishant: adding tests to simulate 2 regions and forced saturations. We'll also add a metric `embedding_dim_mismatch_count` and an alert at >1/min for a customer.

sara_ops: billing note: please hold credits until we confirm impact. I'll prepare a one-time credit and follow-up once eng posts RCA.

ellie_support: formatting short customer-facing summary to send now: "We identified a routing fallback that routed your eu requests to a us variant with a different embedding size when eu capacity was saturated. Temporary mitigation: we pinned your account to eu nodes and increased capacity. Engineers are patching routing to avoid variant-dimension fallbacks and will add validation to return an explicit error if dimensions don't match." Sending now. :white_check_mark:

tim_engineering: ETA for code fix: PR today, canary tomorrow, full rollout after smoke tests (48h).

alex_m: thanks everyone. follow-ups: eng -> PR link in thread, infra -> keep override for 4h, ops -> hold billing credit pending RCA. I'll triage postmortem once incident is quiet. :thumbsup:
